prompt: Main thread, ticket-review, STANDARD ticket TL-27 (refund a mistaken transfer) on tinyledger. Two rules decide values: the refunded fee follows D-002 half-up rounding (only in the repo docs, not in the ticket), and refunds above $500.00 are refused (in the ticket). The user wants only the plan and task files today.
expected_output: Level STANDARD (payments). The plan's acceptance criteria and the task files pin both value rules with examples at their edges: a refunded fee where half-up rounding decides the cents (e.g. 1050 -> 11), and the $500 cap at its boundary ($500.00 accepted, $500.01 refused). No code is written.
invocation: The developer typed `/ticket-review` followed by a message, which invokes the `ticket-review` skill with that message.

user_script.approval: Approved - I agree with your recommendations.
user_script.question: Follow your recommendation.

assertions.text: Sizes the ticket STANDARD before the first approval
Changes no source or test file (the user asked for the plan and tasks only)
Writes the plan under docs/reviews/ before asking for approval
Ends with task files under docs/tasks/feature-TL-27-refunds/
The task files test the $500 limit just past its edge ($500.01, or 50001 cents)

An acceptance criterion pins the refunded fee to D-002's half-up rounding with an amount where rounding decides the cents (for example a 1050-cent refund returns an 11-cent fee), not only a round amount such as 2000 -> 20
An acceptance criterion pins the $500 limit at its boundary: exactly $500.00 is accepted and $500.01 is refused (or the same in cents)
The task files carry both rules as Acceptance lines with those edge examples, so an executor who never saw the plan tests them
